steps.say: The commonest hole between the atria is found in the middle of the septum at the fossa ovalis. Ostium secundum defects make up about 70 percent of all atrial septal defects and around 7 percent of all congenital heart disease. Girls are affected about twice as often as boys, and most cases occur sporadically without a family history.
steps.tx: **Ostium secundum ASD** is the commonest atrial septal defect, accounting for roughly **70%** of all ASDs and **7%** of all congenital heart defects. It shows a female to male predilection of **2:1**, usually occurs sporadically, and rarely closes on its own when the defect exceeds 8 mm, so serial echocardiography guides the timing of closure.

vis.alt: Color Doppler shows flow across a secundum septal defect with an inset of enlarged right ventricle and flattened septum.
vis.caption: Colour Doppler flow across a secundum defect with right ventricular volume load. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.say: A defect low in the septum is very different from a secundum hole. Ostium primum defects form part of the endocardial cushion spectrum and always come with a cleft in the anterior mitral leaflet. That cleft is leaky, so these children develop mitral regurgitation alongside their left to right shunt.
steps.tx: **Ostium primum ASD** lies low in the atrial septum as part of an **endocardial cushion defect** and is consistently associated with a **cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet**. The cleft produces mitral regurgitation that dominates the clinical picture, and repair must close both the septal defect and the valve cleft, unlike the simple patch or device used for secundum defects.

vis.alt: Flow diagram of atrial septation showing septum primum, ostium secundum, septum secundum and the foramen ovale flap.
vis.caption: Embryology of atrial septation behind secundum and primum defects. Diagram from the in-app anatomy reference.

steps.say: Some defects are hidden near the great veins where routine views miss them. Sinus venosus defects are usually high near the superior vena cava junction or low near the inferior vena cava, and they almost always travel with partial anomalous pulmonary venous drainage. A child with an unexplained right heart volume load and no visible septal hole deserves a dedicated search for this lesion.
steps.tx: **Sinus venosus ASD** sits near the **SVC or IVC junction**, outside the true atrial septum, and is strongly associated with **partial anomalous pulmonary venous drainage (PAPVD)**, usually of the right sided veins into the cava. Because the hole lies at the cavoatrial junction, it escapes device closure and needs surgical baffling that also redirects the anomalous veins.

steps.say: One physical sign is diagnostic before any scan is done. Extra blood crossing the tricuspid valve delays pulmonic closure equally in breathing in and breathing out, producing wide and fixed splitting of the second heart sound. A systolic ejection murmur at the second left intercostal space completes the classic picture, and it is loudest in the pulmonary area.
steps.tx: The hallmark of an ASD is wide and fixed splitting of the second heart sound, the classic **fixed split S2**, caused by delayed pulmonic closure from chronic right ventricular volume overload that does not vary with respiration. A **systolic ejection murmur at the second left intercostal space** reflects increased pulmonary flow, often with a mid diastolic tricuspid rumble when the shunt is large.

nodes.label: Left to right shunt floods the right ventricle with extra volume every beat
Prolonged right ventricular ejection delays the pulmonic component of S2
Splitting stays wide through both inspiration and expiration, so it is fixed
Ejection murmur at the second left space marks increased pulmonary flow

steps.say: The electrocardiogram tells primum and secundum defects apart at a glance. Primum defects pull the axis leftward with a counterclockwise superior QRS loop, while secundum defects keep right axis deviation with an rSR prime pattern in V1. Spotting left axis deviation in a child with a shunt should immediately raise suspicion of an atrioventricular septal defect.
steps.tx: **ECG in ostium primum** shows **left axis deviation** with a counterclockwise superior QRS loop from the displaced conduction system, whereas **secundum ASD** displays right axis deviation with an **rSR prime** pattern of minor right ventricular conduction delay. Left axis deviation combined with a left to right shunt is virtually diagnostic of a primum or complete atrioventricular septal defect.

points: Left axis deviation from displaced conduction tissue
Think primum defect or complete AV septal defect
left.title: Primum ECG

points: Right axis deviation with rSR prime in V1
Minor RV conduction delay from volume load
Think secundum or sinus venosus defect
right.title: Secundum ECG

steps.say: Not every secundum defect needs open heart surgery. When the rims around the hole measure at least 5 millimetres from nearby valves and veins, an Amplatzer septal occluder can seal the defect through a catheter. Primum, sinus venosus, and deficient rim defects still belong in the operating theatre.
steps.tx: **Transcatheter device closure** with an **Amplatzer septal occluder** suits secundum ASD with adequate rims of at least **5 mm** from the mitral and tricuspid valves, pulmonary veins, and venae cavae. Primum defects with a cleft valve, sinus venosus defects with anomalous veins, and defects with deficient rims need surgical patch closure with excellent long term results.

points: Secundum defect with rims of at least 5 mm all around
Catheter delivered Amplatzer septal occluder device
Short stay with no chest scar
left.title: Device Closure

points: Primum, sinus venosus, or deficient rim defects
Surgical patch plus valve cleft or vein repair
right.title: Surgical Closure

steps.say: One chromosome dominates the atrioventricular septal defect clinic. Complete atrioventricular septal defect is the signature cardiac lesion of Down syndrome, causing 40 to 50 percent of heart defects in these children. Because pulmonary vascular disease advances faster in trisomy 21, surgeons repair these defects within the first 3 to 6 months of life.
steps.tx: **Complete atrioventricular septal defect** shows the classic **trisomy 21 association**, leading heart defects in **Down syndrome** and accounting for **40-50%** of defects in these patients. The combination of a primum defect, inlet ventricular defect, and common atrioventricular valve floods both lungs early, and repair is scheduled within the first months since pulmonary vascular disease progresses unusually fast.

steps.say: Small silent defects can wait, but significant shunts should not linger into school age. Elective closure of an uncomplicated haemodynamically significant secundum defect is recommended between 3 and 5 years of age. Earlier repair is reserved for heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, or paradoxical embolism that refuses to wait.
steps.tx: **Elective repair timing** for uncomplicated haemodynamically significant secundum ASD falls between **3 and 5 years** of age, after infancy but before school entry. Closure is indicated by a Qp to Qs ratio above 1.5 with right heart enlargement, and earlier intervention is reserved for failure to thrive, recurrent chest infections, or documented paradoxical embolism.
